response:
Diagnosis: the search has converged on a coherent economic story with two distinct, empirically validated ingredients. First, valuation legs built on *unencumbered claims* — net current assets less all liabilities, optionally rank-combined with a recurring cash-earnings claim — carry FF5 alpha that conventional equity yields do not; the rank-weighted stock-and-flow claim version is now the archive's best joint result (fmb 5.57, alpha +2.4%, t 2.21, Sharpe 0.375). Second, and newly, the *survival-horizon* channel works: cash measured against the annual operating cost base delivered alpha +2.9% with t 3.21 and Sharpe 0.29 at coverage 0.138, the cleanest reliability in the archive. Both say the same thing — a discount converts into return when the firm cannot be forced to transact (liquidate, refinance, or dilute) before the discount closes. Channels that failed are equally informative: payout verification (+0.1%), asset-turnover quality (−2.5%), accrual conservatism (+0.3%) and hidden depreciation (−2.0%) all add nothing. This generation consolidates the claim and runway channels together (S1, S2), pins down the correct runway definition (S3), tests whether runway can rescue a value leg known to produce negative alpha (S5), extends the forced-transaction logic to the short side (S6), and explores one genuinely new mechanism — cash held relative to the firm's own precautionary need (S4).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Claim Cheapness With Survival Horizon
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: A discount is realised by shareholders when the firm owns an unencumbered claim larger than its price and can also fund its operating cost base from cash on hand, because such a firm chooses when to transact rather than being forced by creditors or a cash shortfall.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This unites the archive's two strongest and economically complementary results — the rank-weighted stock-and-flow claim valuation leg (fmb 5.57, alpha +2.4%) and the operating cash runway quality leg (alpha +2.9%, t 3.21) — which describe the same forced-transaction mechanism from the asset side and the liquidity side respectively. Because the runway leg uses cash against cost of goods sold while the valuation leg uses net current assets against price, the two are far less mechanically entangled than the profitability screens tried previously.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Claim Cheapness With Profit And Runway
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3), RATIO(che, cogs))))
HYPOTHESIS: Earning power and survival horizon are separate guarantees behind a discounted claim — one says the business creates value, the other says it will still be standing when the market notices — and a cheap firm offering both should outperform one offering either alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gross profitability and cash runway have each independently produced positive alpha against claim-based valuation legs, and combining them at equal rank weight inside a single quality rank tests additivity without the double multiplicative shrinkage that would concentrate the long leg in an unstably small corner. Against Signal 1 it isolates whether profitability still contributes once survival horizon is controlled, which is the open question left by the archive's profitability screens.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cheapness With Working Capital Runway
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: The relevant survival horizon is not cash alone but all near-term resources net of near-term obligations, since receivables collect and inventory sells within the operating cycle while payables come due within it; measured against the annual cost base this is the true number of months a cheap firm can operate without external capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The runway channel is the newest strong result in the archive and its definition has been tested only once, in its narrowest cash-only form; broadening the numerator to net working capital while holding the valuation leg fixed identifies whether the mechanism is literal cash on hand or the whole self-funding operating cycle. Both variants have near-universal coverage, so any difference in alpha is attributable to the economics rather than to sample composition.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cheapness With Cash Beyond Precautionary Need
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(RATIO(che, at), VOL(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: How much cash a firm needs depends on how uncertain its cash flows are; a cheap firm holding far more cash than its own earnings volatility justifies is carrying an unrecognised distributable asset, whereas the same cash balance in a volatile business is merely a required buffer and adds no value to shareholders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the one genuinely new mechanism in the batch: it scales the liquidity channel by the firm's own precautionary requirement rather than by its cost base, so it distinguishes excess cash from necessary cash — a distinction no archived signal makes and that the corporate cash-holdings literature says drives the market's valuation of a dollar of cash. The ratio is strictly positive in both numerator and denominator, so it is monotone with no sign discontinuity, at the cost of requiring five years of history.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Gross Profit Yield With Survival Horizon
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross-profit-to-price identifies firms priced cheaply against their earning power, but that discount is only collectible by shareholders who are not diluted first; conditioning it on the firm's cash runway should convert a spread that factor models fully explain into one they do not.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gross-profit-to-price has repeatedly delivered the archive's largest Fama-MacBeth slopes (4.5 to 5.7) alongside zero-to-negative FF5 alpha, meaning HML and RMW price it completely; pairing it with the runway screen tests directly whether forced-dilution risk is the reason the factor-explained portion of value earns nothing abnormal. A positive result would show the runway channel is portable across valuation legs rather than specific to balance-sheet claims, which would materially generalise the mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Rich Price With Debt Due And No Cash
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(dlc, che)))
HYPOTHESIS: The mirror of the survival-horizon premium is a forced-transaction penalty: a firm whose price is high relative to a negative net liquid claim and whose current debt dwarfs its cash must refinance or issue equity on someone else's terms, transferring value away from existing shareholders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Prior short-side attempts produced correct-signed alphas but wrong-signed cross-sectional slopes whenever the valuation leg was oriented toward high book-to-market; orienting it toward expensiveness relative to the liquid claim aligns both statistics, as the archive's rich-price-strained-balance-sheet result began to show. Scaling current debt by cash rather than by current assets targets the specific rollover moment when refinancing must happen, complementing rather than repeating the earlier maturity-cliff test.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Claim Cheapness With Survival Horizon---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A clean, internally consistent pairing of the archive's two best-performing legs (the stock-and-flow claim yield and the che/cogs runway screen) with genuinely distinct inputs, though it is a recombination of existing components rather than a new mechanism, so the incremental information over the two parents may be small.

---CRITIQUE Claim Cheapness With Profit And Runway---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially Signal 1 with gross profitability averaged into the quality rank — a cosmetic superset that structurally repeats the archived "Net Cash Cheapness With Dual Quality Screen" template, and equal-weight rank blending will dilute rather than isolate whichever leg is actually driving the alpha.

---CRITIQUE Cheapness With Working Capital Runway---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated mechanism (survival horizon) does not match what (act−lct)/cogs measures — net working capital is largely inventory and receivables, i.e. the same bloat that the archive's working-capital and accrual signals price *negatively* — so the expected positive sign is economically contestable and the construction is otherwise a one-input tweak of the archived cash-runway signal.

---CRITIQUE Cheapness With Cash Beyond Precautionary Need---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Scaling cash by the firm's own cash-flow volatility to separate excess from precautionary cash is the only genuinely new economic state variable in the batch, ranking neutralises the ratio's fat tail, and it sits close to but not on top of the known cash-holdings/idiosyncratic-volatility literature — worth testing, with the caveat that the 5-year VOL requirement will bite coverage and the result may partly reload on low-volatility exposure.

---CRITIQUE Gross Profit Yield With Survival Horizon---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A legitimate portability test of the runway channel against the valuation leg that has repeatedly shown strong FMB slopes with zero FF5 alpha, but it shares the entire quality leg with Signal 1 and the GP/P × IND_RANK(quality) template has already failed on alpha five times in this archive, so the prior is weak.

---CRITIQUE Rich Price With Debt Due And No Cash---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The short-side orientation and the dlc/che rollover ratio are correctly signed and coherently motivated as a fix for the sign misalignment in the archived refinancing-cliff test, but it recombines two archived signals' parts and dlc/che is undefined or explosive for near-zero-cash firms, which will concentrate the short leg in a small, unstable set that IND_RANK only partly tames.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Claim Cheapness With Creditor-Proof Cash
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(dltt, dlc))))
HYPOTHESIS: Two different agents can force a cheap firm to transact before its discount closes — its operations, by consuming cash, and its creditors, by demanding repayment — and cash measured against total interest-bearing debt tests the second channel: a firm that could extinguish its entire debt from cash on hand answers to no lender.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Rather than averaging profitability into an existing quality rank, this substitutes a different denominator for the liquidity buffer and thereby separates the two economically distinct forced-transaction risks, so a comparison with the accepted cost-base runway signal identifies which one the alpha actually comes from. Cash-to-debt is not a leverage ratio in disguise because debt-free firms and cash-rich levered firms are ordered by their ability to retire claims outright, and both inputs are universally reported so coverage stays in the high tier.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Cheapness With A Durable Liquidity Policy
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(che, cogs), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap firm's liquidity is a quality attribute only if it is a standing policy rather than a recent event: a firm whose worst cash-to-operating-cost ratio over five years was still comfortable has structurally chosen to be unforced, whereas a firm whose buffer is high today but was thin two years ago has simply just raised capital and remains dependent on markets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the contested net-working-capital numerator — which the archive prices negatively as inventory and receivable bloat — and instead keeps the validated cash-to-cost measure while changing the moment of the distribution from current level to five-year trough. Unlike the earlier through-cycle attempt, the quality leg shares no accounting quantity with the book-to-market valuation leg, so the product genuinely gates cheapness on an independent liquidity-policy state rather than squaring one balance-sheet item.
REASONING_END
